{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZcAX7g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDDPws", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 55, "title": "Preserve unread 8253 counter snapshots across repeated latch commands", "body": "## Problem

Repeated ordinary PIT counter-latch commands overwrite an unread snapshot and restart its byte sequence. This breaks stable guest timer reads, including a paired read interrupted by another latch command.

At baseline `9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618`, [Pit::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618/src/devices.rs#L369) unconditionally assigns `latch` and clears `read_hi`. [Counter::read](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618/src/devices.rs#L215) otherwise retains a paired snapshot until its second byte is consumed.

Implement this missing latch behavior as one bounded improvement to the existing binary modes. Reliable counter readout supports guest timing and calibration across both machine profiles.

## Expected outcome

For ordinary latch commands selecting counter 0, 1 or 2 with D5:D4=`00`:

- Capture the current count when no snapshot is pending.
- Ignore further latch commands until that snapshot is completely read, preserving both its value and the next unread byte.
- Release the snapshot after the programmed one-byte or two-byte read; a subsequent latch captures a new count.
- Preserve ongoing counting, mode, reload, OUT and unrelated counters.

Intel’s [8253/8253-5 datasheet, Read Operations and Reading While Counting](https://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~mpj/llp/references/8253.pdf) specifies stable latched reads and completion of the programmed read sequence. Intel’s [8254 datasheet, printed pages 7–8](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/23wi-cs212/pintos/specs/8254.pdf#page=7) explicitly specifies ignoring duplicate latch commands until consumption. Applying this rule to the ordinary 8253 latch command is the shared-behavior interpretation used here; Intel identifies the 8254 as an 8253 superset on page 1. This does not introduce the separate 8254 read-back command.

Scope is latch retention in existing binary modes 0, 2 and 3, including existing mode aliases, all counters and both mapped port banks. Preserve existing fresh-mode and Machine-reset behavior. Non-goals include new counting modes, BCD, external GATE, arbitrary latch insertion into unfinished unlatched reads, and new interleaved count-write semantics.

## Context and reproduction

These are source-derived reproductions, not evaluator-executed tests. Use the existing `Clock` helper in [tests/pit.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618/tests/pit.rs#L1) to advance exact PIT clocks:

1. Program counter 0, paired binary mode 0, count `1234h`; advance its initial load clock. Latch, advance `100h` clocks and latch again before reading. Expected bytes: `34h,12h`; the current source produces `34h,11h`.
2. Start independently with the same programming. Latch and read `34h`; advance `101h` clocks and latch again. The next byte must remain `12h`. The current source restarts at the replacement low byte, `33h`.
3. After fully consuming either original snapshot, latch again without advancing time and verify the current count. This distinguishes retention from a latch that never releases.

Existing tests cover frozen snapshots during counting and divisor replacement, including half-consumed snapshots, but do not exercise another latch command while one remains pending. Relevant examples are `ordinary_latched_read_is_frozen_while_counting_continues`, `mode3_latched_reads_continue_counting_through_both_halves`, and `mode0_rewrite_preserves_completed_latch_snapshots`.

Project progress: PR #54 is merged at this baseline. Its [Coordinator validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618/docs/validation.md#issue-53-mode-3-count-only-rewrites-at-half-cycle-boundaries-2026-10-24) reports 14 focused rewrite tests, 56 PIT tests, 216 native integration tests and 82 production-Wasm browser tests passing. Independent review and remote CI are not established by the supplied report. The evaluator inspected source and reports without executing acceptance. The supplied open-issue list is empty; this behavior is distinct from the completed divisor-rewrite improvements.

All 26 supplied inventory statuses and fixed scopes remain unchanged. Partial: cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio, integration. Unimplemented: paging, fpu, rtc. Implemented but unverified: ide, grcg. No category is verified.

PIT work remaining beyond this Issue includes modes 1/4/5, external gates/retriggering, BCD, mode-2/3 divisor-1 policy, other access-sequencing cases, non-mode-3 beeper behavior and audio sampling across scheduler batches. Protected execution, paging and basic FPU remain required project goals. Limited probes and six-game reports establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add focused original Rust tests under a `counter_latch_` prefix. Record both reproductions failing on the unchanged production baseline and passing after the implementation.
- [ ] Cover repeated commands before any read and between paired bytes; multiple ignored commands; LSB-only, MSB-only and paired formats; release and fresh capture; all counters; modes 0/2/3 and existing aliases; zero-encoded count; and channel isolation. Use byte-distinct snapshots so accidental replacement or byte restart cannot pass.
- [ ] Exercise VM and Ap through both port banks, including issuing a command through one bank and consuming it through the other. Verify unchanged count/OUT progression and IRQ behavior against an otherwise identical control, plus cancellation by fresh supported-mode programming and Machine reset.
- [ ] Add a separate original MIT source-built boot probe exercising both duplicate-command cases and successful recapture through guest port I/O. Provide offline assembly/preparation and a checked provenance manifest containing source/license, assembly command, hashes, result bytes, guards and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget. Keep generated fixtures outside `web/` and prepare the new fixture in CI.
- [ ] Run that same image natively and through production-release Wasm on VM and Ap, before and after reset, at browser roots `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require explicit PASS, no FAIL/core/browser errors, exact results and guards, and unchanged disk bytes. The host may step and observe; it must not manufacture guest results or timer events.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test pit counter_latch_`, the complete PIT target, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`, following [README fixture preparation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9156f727d928ceb938c7d20a1dc24425e416e618/README.md#reproduce-the-checks). Preserve existing hardware, CPU-shadow, BIOS timer, DOS/app, VM and game assertions, fixtures and execution budgets. Use original or licensed tests with explicit provenance; acquire no commercial ROMs or proprietary guest software.
- [ ] Update the bounded hardware contract and validation record with exact commands, outcomes and limitations. Complete review and resolve blocking findings before merge; retain PIT’s partial status and all deferred category scopes.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
